dutyCycle.notes: Generic worked example illustrating the duty-cycle concept: 3 minutes welding, 7 minutes resting within a 10-minute period. Not tied to a specific process or the OmniPro 220's actual rated duty cycle on this page.

polarity.notes: Connect MIG gun to wire feed; connect wire feed control inside welder.
Follow MIG cable setup but reverse: ground clamp to positive terminal, wire feed power to negative terminal.
Connect gas line to gas regulator; connect foot pedal inside welder; leave wire feed power disconnected.

settings.notes: Skill level: Low. Applications: galvanized steel, general fabrication, pipe and tubing, maintenance & repair. Weld result: more spatter. Uses cored wire; welds over mill scale and rust; requires minimal surface prep; usable outdoor in windy conditions; deep weld penetration, handles material gaps well.

settings.material: Steel, Stainless steel, Aluminum (spool gun required)
settings.notes: Skill level: Low. Applications: sheet metal, automotive body, tubing, structural steel. Weld result: clean/minimal spatter. Uses solid wire; uses shielding gas; clean welds with minimal spatter; good for thin materials like sheet metal.
Skill level: Moderate. Applications: pipe and tubing, structural steel, pressure vessels, maintenance & repair. Weld result: more spatter. Deep penetration; good choice for thicker materials.

settings.material: Steel, Stainless steel, Chrome moly (DC TIG required); Aluminum, Magnesium alloys (AC TIG required)
settings.notes: Skill level: High. Applications: stainless steel exhausts, bicycle frames, thin wall pipe & tubing, metal art. Weld result: extremely clean. Highest quality welds, precise control.

setupSteps.process: Wire spool install & wire-feed check (MIG/Flux-Core, general power-on sequence)
steps: Connect cables as needed for flux wire welding (see back of guide for process-specific cable setup).
Install wire spool. Insert wire through both feed guides and clamp it into feed mechanism. See manual if changing wire size or using solid wire.
Take off nozzle and tip, plug selected cord into welder and into wall, turn welder on, and press cold wire feed switch until wire comes out.
Incrementally tighten wire feed tension knob clockwise until wire will bend from feed tension at 2"-3".
Unplug welder and replace nozzle and tip.
Hold gun clear of workpiece, then plug in welder, turn it on, and set weld thickness and other settings.
Connect ground clamp to negative terminal.
Connect electrode holder to positive terminal.
Connect ground clamp to negative terminal.
Connect wire feed power to positive terminal.
Connect MIG gun to wire feed.
Connect wire feed control inside welder.
Follow MIG cable setup but connect ground clamp to positive terminal and wire feed power to negative terminal.
Connect ground clamp to positive terminal.
Connect TIG torch to negative terminal.
Connect gas line to gas regulator.
